name: Alternating Lat Pulldown Behind Neck
description: The alternating behind-neck pulldown alternates each rep between pulling to the front (standard) and pulling behind the neck, targeting the lats and trapezius from slightly different angles within a single set. The behind-neck portion challenges the lower traps and upper rhomboids through a downward-angled scapular depression that the front pulldown angle does not fully replicate.

execution.starting_position: Seated at a lat pulldown station with a wide grip bar. Arms extended overhead gripping the bar.
execution.setup_instructions: Use lighter weight than usual — behind-neck pulldowns have a shorter range of motion and require careful neck positioning.
steps: Step 1: Pull rep 1 to the front of the chest (standard pulldown).
Step 3: Pull rep 2 behind the neck — tilt the head forward slightly to avoid contact.
Step 5: Alternate front and behind-neck for the duration of the set.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on each pull. Inhale on each return.
common_mistakes: Not tilting the head forward for the behind-neck pull — risks cervical spine impingement
Using heavy weight for the behind-neck portion — this is a moderate-load variation
safety_considerations: The behind-neck pulldown is contraindicated for those with cervical spine issues
Always tilt the head forward — never pull the bar into the neck
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to full lat contraction on each variation.
coaching_cues: Same lat drive regardless of direction
Control the bar path — do not let it pull back up
